headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors because CrewAI writes/reads shared files while Argo Workflows can pass artifacts and parameters into downstream steps.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can pass artifacts and parameters between steps, and CrewAI reads/writes the host working directory with stdin/stdout and file I/O. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge where attacker-controlled workflow outputs could be interpreted by CrewAI as directives. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF Argo outputs untrusted text into an artifact or parameter consumed by CrewAI
IF CrewAI agents parse file or stdout content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in workflow outputs
Whitelist only structured JSON inputs to CrewAI
Disable automatic tool execution on file contents
Review one sample handoff for prompt-like strings
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between workflow artifacts and agent prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters, while CrewAI reads and writes the host working directory and sends data to model providers and tool integrations. If both run on the same host or workspace, sensitive artifacts can flow from Argo into CrewAI and then out to third-party APIs. This is a default-path concern, though the exact deployment is not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents share a host directory or mounted workspace
IF CrewAI forwards file contents or crew context to model providers or tools
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Restrict CrewAI to redacted inputs only
Rotate and scope API keys used by CrewAI
Inspect one workflow for secret-bearing artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo can orchestrate workflows over APIs and artifacts, while CrewAI can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write files in the host working directory. Overlapping write authority on shared resources can cause races or clobbered outputs even without git modification. The profiles do not show locking, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or artifact path
IF Argo and CrewAI run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint output paths
Serialize writes with a lock file
Run one agent per container
Check for path collisions in one workflow run
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo can emit artifacts and parameters that CrewAI may consume as inputs, and CrewAI can then act via shell, subprocess, or external tools. If CrewAI treats upstream outputs as authoritative, a single bad Argo step can cascade into incorrect downstream actions or irreversible side effects. Because the pair lacks built-in verification in the profiles, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF CrewAI uses Argo-produced artifacts as authoritative task inputs
IF downstream CrewAI tools can send emails, modify systems, or trigger deployments
mitigations: Insert a human review gate before action steps
Require schema validation on all upstream outputs
Mark Argo outputs as untrusted by default
Test one end-to-end run with a benign payload
requires-engineering: add verification and rollback controls

E_compliance.rationale: Argo is an open-source workflow engine with allowlisted egress, while CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data plus API keys and broad egress. If regulated data is placed into a crew or workflow artifact, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches through model-provider calls and host-file storage. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so medium is the prudent choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed into CrewAI crews or Argo artifacts
IF the deployment requires residency, retention, or deletion guarantees not enforced by both agents
mitigations: Classify data before handing it to either agent
Block regulated data from crew inputs
Set short retention on workflow artifacts
Review provider/data-processing terms once
requires-engineering: implement residency and deletion controls
